features.title: Know what an agent is missing before you run it
features.body:
When something an agent uses goes missing, the new app now tells you before a run fails. The item shows **Needs setup** in the agent editor, with the reason under it. If the model can't run, a banner above the chat box says so, and Send stays off until you set it up.

- A missing MCP server, secret or connected app no longer stops a run. The agent runs without it.
- A scheduled or event run whose model needs setup is recorded once as skipped, instead of being retried five times.
- Invite links open in the new app, and new teammates land in the project they were invited to.

features.title: Less repeated work when agent runs start and finish
features.body:
The runner now avoids several repeated steps when starting an agent session. It reuses local tool binaries and Pi skill copies where applicable, mounts drives in parallel, and reuses a harness capability probe.

When its trace is ready, a completed Pi turn no longer waits for the full trace-drain polling window. Organization owners and admins can test their connections from a project that does not use them. Conversation replay no longer cuts through a character and leaves a chat unable to continue.

features.title: First-agent onboarding and more dependable event automations
features.body:
New accounts now enter first-agent onboarding when their project has no agents. The questions use the same role, company-size and referral choices as the signup survey, so people do not need to answer conflicting versions of them.

- Event automations now receive Composio V3 webhook events instead of silently dropping them.
- Editing an automation's event filters now updates its Composio trigger.
- Organizations replace workspace records; self-hosted operators should read the upgrade notes before deploying.

features.title: Use AI provider connections across an organization
features.body:
Organization owners and admins can now add an AI provider connection once for the organization instead of saving the same credential in every project. In Settings, the **Organization** tab shows the connections available to the current project.

- Choose which projects may use a connection; selecting individual projects requires the supported Enterprise entitlement.
- Pick an organization connection explicitly in an agent's model picker.
- Agent runs using a saved bare model ID now mark the matching model row as selected.

features.title: Security updates and agent-run fixes
features.body:
This release updates vulnerable dependencies across the web app, API, SDK and runner.

On self-hosted setups that override `HOME`, Codex runs no longer wait indefinitely on their first turn. Agent runs send the correct project even without an authorization header. The model picker shows a readable Kimi K3.1 Pro label, and session names no longer show a lock icon.

features.title: Continue channel chats in Agenta
features.body:
You can now continue a Slack or Telegram chat in Agenta. Members who can send to a project-visible channel chat can write in the app, and the agent's answer also goes back to the channel thread.

- A private agent can stay connected to a channel through a connection its owner made.
- A new channel chat with that private agent belongs to its owner and starts private.
- Fixes keep first messages and more of a long turn's work when a chat changes or a turn ends.

features.title: More reliable built-in Gemini runs
features.body:
Built-in Gemini agent runs now use Google's native protocol instead of its OpenAI-compatible endpoint. This changes the route used for model calls that could stall on follow-up turns.

Bedrock and SageMaker credentials now travel with each call instead of being set in the shared process environment. The Python SDK also accepts an `AGENTA_API_URL` without a URL scheme, and CSV preview comments no longer show a stray colon when a column has no header.

features.title: Private agents and chats, and sharing with your project
features.body:
New chats and agents that you create in Agenta now start private. Only you see them until you share them. You can share a chat with chosen people as **Can view** or **Can send**, or make it visible to the whole project. You can also make an agent private.

Chats and agents that existed before this release keep working as before. They are visible to the project, with their creator as owner.

improvements.text: Claude Haiku 5.5 is available for agents, also on Pi
Built-in Gemini models use Google's native protocol

fixes.text: Stop keeps the partial answer and ends the turn as stopped
A message that you send stays when you switch to another chat
You can write to channel chats in the app, and private agents stay connected to their channels
A turn that reaches its time limit keeps the work it did
Long turns are no longer cut short by the output budget

features.title: Projects use only their own provider keys
features.body:
Prompts and evaluators now run on the provider keys saved in the project. A project without a key for a provider gets the error "No API key found for model". Add the key in **Settings > Providers & Models**.

Custom providers need their own API key, except Bedrock, SageMaker and Vertex. Self-hosted Enterprise deployments can opt in to keys set on the services container.

improvements.text: Built-in Gemini uses gemini-3.8-flash with low thinking by default

fixes.text: Built-in Gemini turns no longer hang when a Vertex call stalls
Gmail addresses with dots or a +tag count as one address at sign-up

features.title: Project access, permissions and runs that act as their creator
features.body:
Agenta now decides project access in one place. Creating, renaming and deleting a project follows organization roles. An API key acts only in its own project for management actions. When you remove a member or delete a key, the change takes effect at the next request.

Automations, evaluations and approvals run as the user or key that created them. If that identity loses access, the run stops and tells you why.

improvements.text: Agenta checks organization admin rights, SSO domains, credentials and password resets more strictly

fixes.text: The membership repair migration stays fast on large databases
